newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: NEW LISTING LIFTS ZIMBABWE STOCKS TO RECORD LEVELS.
newsitem.headline: NEW LISTING LIFTS ZIMBABWE STOCKS TO RECORD LEVELS.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares scaled new peaks on Thursday, lifted by a rash of intense trading which brokers said was largely inspired by the debut on the local bourse of local vegetable company Interfresh.
The main industrial index leapt 111.16 points -- or one percent -- to break through the key 10,900 barrier ending at a historic high of 10,980.10.
"The Interfresh listing was the big feature today. It created a lot of excitement and intense trading on the exchange today which saw the industrial index moving higher," a broker said.
The brokers said Interfresh debuted with bids at 240 cents, sellers at 260 cents and deals opened at 240 then 250 cents with 15 million shares changing hands.

Brokers said they expected the bourse to continue bullish on Friday but added that foreigners were likely to be a bit wary following the reintroduction on Wednesday of foreign exchange controls on dual-listed stocks.

Among Thursday's winners, merchant banker FMB jumped 100 cents to 5,100, hotel and supermarket group Meikles rose 50 cents to 2,950, tea producer Tanganda gained 40 cents to 600 and blue-chip beverages and supermarket conglomerate Delta put on 15 cents to 1,825.
Against the trend, rubber and agricultural products manufacturer Acacia dropped 30 cents to 320 and Alloys shed 25 cents to 500.
Minings were quiet with gold producers Falgold and Rio Tinto unchanged while copper miner Mhangura rose eight cents to 30.
The secondary mining index edged up a marginal 0.73 points to 1,014.88.
